Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Moneo issue #227: configurable speech-to-text for the CHAT MIC only. Voice calls and GPT-Live stay untouched. **PR 1 is merged** (#267): it added the engine contract in `lib/ai/speech/`, `POST /api/voice/transcribe` for batch engines, the fallback to OpenAI with a `fellBack` note, and Settings → Voice → "Speech to text", stored as `workspace_settings.speech_engine`. Read that code first. You build **PR 2: the "On this computer" engine.**

The owner agreed this design:
- **Runtime.** transformers.js (`@huggingface/transformers`) with onnxruntime-node, running on the Moneo server in a worker thread so requests stay responsive. Load the model on first use and unload it after an idle timeout. Pass the vocabulary hints from `lib/ai/voice-vocabulary.ts` as the prompt or initial text, where the model supports it.
- **Suggested models in Settings,** each with size, languages and speed: Moonshine Base (~60 MB, English, very fast), Whisper Base (~150 MB, multilingual incl. German), Whisper Small (~500 MB, multilingual, best quality) and Distil-Whisper (English).
  - Each one has a **Download** button. It saves the model into Moneo's data folder (desktop: under `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` / the app data dir; source install: a git-ignored `.data/` path) and shows progress.
  - A **Choose file…** option takes a model the owner already has. On desktop this is a native dialog through `lib/desktop-bridge.ts` and `desktop/src/bridge.ts`. On the source install it's a path field.
  - A **Try it** button: say a sentence and see the text.
- **Audio stays on the machine.** It works from the phone too, because the model runs on the computer.
- **Fallback.** If the model is missing or fails and an OpenAI key exists, PR 1's rule applies: use OpenAI and show the note.
- **Desktop.** Add the native module to `electron-builder.config.cjs`, add the models folder to backup and restore only if that's appropriate (models are re-downloadable, so probably exclude them and say why), and check whether `fetch-backend.mjs` needs changes. See AGENTS.md → Desktop app.
  - Files read at runtime by a dynamic path need `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/`.
  - Keep the security fuses.
  - The Desktop workflow must pass on all four platforms. Apple Silicon runners are scarce: if a job is cancelled for lack of a runner, rerun it with `gh run rerun <id> --failed` once the run has finished.
- **Source install.** It must work with plain `npm ci`. Update README.md (how to download and choose a model) and `.env.example` if you add a variable.
- **Reset all data** clears the engine choice but never deletes model files.
- **Tests.** Engine selection with a fake model runner, the download manager (fake fetch, resume or verify by size/hash), and route behaviour. Never download a real model in `npm test`. A real-model check can be a manual script you run once and report.
- **Not in this PR:** live words while speaking. That's PR 4, stacked later.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 227 --comments` and PR #267.
- Branch `t3/issue-227-local-engine` from current `origin/main`. Commit each step, ending each message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Don't end your turn while a command or CI run is still going.** Wait in the same turn.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start yourself in this session, verified by PID.**
- Run one `npm ci` at a time. If it stalls, retry once with `--prefer-offline`.
- The QA app on port 3100 and the moneo-qa backend are shared:
  - never run `npm run qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`;
  - never touch the owner's backend;
  - revert any migration you apply to QA.
- Never test against the owner's installed desktop app. Set `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` to a scratch folder.
- Any migration needs a unique prefix later than the newest file in supabase/migrations on origin/main.
- **Run `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` yourself and quote their last lines in your final reply.** Also run `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run check:bundle`.
- Use the verify-ui skill for Settings (light/dark/mobile). Link the screenshots in the PR body from a commit, then remove them from the branch.
- Push and open a PR to `main`. The body says "Part 2 of #227" (don't close the issue) and ends with:

  Never merge.

{"body":"Part 1 of #227 (does not close it).

## What changed

The chat mic's speech-to-text is now an engine behind one contract; later parts add "On this computer" and OpenRouter on top. Voice calls (GPT-Live) are untouched.

- **Contract** (`lib/ai/speech/`): batch engines take recorded audio plus hints (prompt and workspace names) and return text. `chooseSpeechEngine` and `transcribeWithFallback` are pure and take the engines as arguments: if the chosen engine is unavailable or fails and an OpenAI key exists, OpenAI is used and the result says so (`fellBack`); with no key the caller gets a clear reason. OpenAI is never retried against itself.
- **OpenAI**: live streaming is unchanged (same `gpt-live-transcribe` session and vocabulary hints). OpenAI is also registered as a batch engine (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`) so it can be the fallback when a batch engine fails.
- **Routes**: `POST /api/voice/session` now resolves the engine and returns `mode: "live"` (token, as before) or `mode: "batch"`. New `POST /api/voice/transcribe` takes raw PCM16 (`audio/pcm` + `?rate=`) or WAV, limited to 12 MB, validated with Zod, owner-authenticated, and calls the registry.
- **Client**: live engines stream as before. Batch engines record, then post once on Send/Done; Send/Done UX is unchanged. A small note shows in the mic UI (while recording and after the words are sent, dismissible) when OpenAI replaced the chosen engine, and a transcription error is shown instead of "Didn't catch that".
- **Settings → Voice**: new section holding the call voice (moved from "AI and your data") and **Speech to text**. Only OpenAI is selectable; "On this computer" and "OpenRouter" are listed as coming soon. Stored as `workspace_settings.speech_engine` (migration `202611160051_speech_engine.sql`, `save_workspace_preferences` updated, `lib/schema.ts` aligned). A value this version can't read falls back to OpenAI without blocking sign-in. Reset all data deletes the settings row, so it clears the choice.
- README line about voice and dictation updated.

## How I verified it

- `npm test`: 306 files passed, 1763 tests passed. New tests cover engine choice and fallback with fake engines, audio encoding/decoding and limits, the transcribe route (auth, validation, size, fallback, error without details), the session route modes, the batch recorder, the fallback note state, the settings preference and its unreadable-value case.
- `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run build` succeeds.
- `lib/schema.live.test.ts` passes against the `moneo-qa` backend (schema matches the migrated database). I also saved the Settings form in the QA app and got "Preferences saved" (so the updated RPC accepts the new field).
- Screenshots of the QA app (`qa:shots`, no console errors or failed requests) in light, dark and mobile:

Not covered:
- `supabase/tests/migrations.mjs` (fresh-schema replay) failed twice with a lock timeout on `pg_namespace` because another checkout's long-running test held the shared QA database. The CI `database` job runs it.
- The real microphone and the note shown while recording, since the QA app has no real AI key. Those paths are covered by the recorder and state-machine tests.

# Verify a change in the running app

The owner reviews what the app does, not the diff. "It compiles" and "the tests pass" are not proof; pictures and recordings of the real app are.

Everything here runs against the QA app on http://localhost:3100. Never use port 3000; that is the owner's app and data.

## 1. Launch

`npm run setup -- --qa`, then `npm run qa:auth`, then `npm run qa:server` in the background. It is ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-moneo-test: 1" http://localhost:3100/api/health` prints 401 or 200.

If port 3100 is already taken, another checkout's QA app owns it and serves that checkout's code. Do not kill it. Start this checkout's app on a free port with `QA_PORT=<port> npm run qa:server` and point the tools at it with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port>`.

## 2. Doctor

Run this whenever anything looks off, before changing code:

`npm run qa:shots -- doctor home`

It fails with the reason when the app is not worth driving:

- **"The QA session was not accepted"**: the saved session expired (they last an hour). Run `npm run qa:auth`.
- **Every page is the "could not sign you in" screen after a fresh `qa:auth`**: the shared QA workspace holds data this checkout cannot read. Run `npm run qa:reset`.
- **A failed request or console error on an untouched page**: the base is broken. Fix or report that first; evidence taken on a broken base proves nothing.

## 3. Drive

1. **List the pages.** Every route the change can affect, including the ones AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" names.
2. **Set up the state.** If a page needs data, create it the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does. An empty page proves an empty page.
3. **Before.** With the change set aside (a temporary commit on another branch, or `git worktree add` of the base):
   `npm run qa:shots -- before home money/transactions`
   Name pages without the leading slash (Git Bash rewrites `/paths`); `home` is `/`.
4. **After.** On the changed code, the same command with `after`.

Each run writes `<page>-light.png`, `<page>-dark.png` and `<page>-mobile.png` to `.qa/shots/<label>/`, prints the HTTP status and every failed request or console error per page, and exits 1 if there were any.

**A flow, not a page.** A screenshot cannot show a tap, a card being accepted or an undo. Extend the journey spec in `e2e/` that already covers the flow and record it:

`npx playwright test e2e/<spec> --workers=1 --trace on --video on`

Add a new spec only when no existing journey can take the check (AGENTS.md Tests).

## 4. Evidence

- Use the path the owner uses: real pages, real buttons. Not a test-only endpoint or a direct database write for the step under test.
- Capture the action and the state it leaves, not only the last screen.
- Check the side effects next to what is visible: the row written, the history entry, what undo restores.
- **Look at every picture yourself.** Read each PNG. Check for overflow, clipped text, unreadable contrast in dark and a broken layout on mobile. A console error or a status of 400 or more is a failure: fix it and shoot again.
- When something looks wrong, suspect the capture before the app, and measure the live page before reporting a bug.

## 5. Hand over

The pictures go in the PR description itself, so the owner sees them on GitHub. A path to `.qa/` is not evidence: it is git-ignored and exists only on this machine. Never commit them to the PR's branch either.

1. Open the PR first to get its number.
2. Push the files to their own branch, `pr-assets/<pr>`, which holds nothing else. The repo is public, so QA data only:

   ```sh
   git worktree add --orphan -b pr-assets/<pr> .qa/pr-assets
   cp -r .qa/shots/before .qa/shots/after .qa/pr-assets/
   git -C .qa/pr-assets add -A
   git -C .qa/pr-assets commit -m "Screenshots for #<pr> (QA data)"
   git -C .qa/pr-assets push origin pr-assets/<pr>
   git worktree remove .qa/pr-assets
   ```

   To add more later, check the branch out again with `git worktree add .qa/pr-assets pr-assets/<pr>`.
3. Embed them with `gh pr edit <pr> --body-file <file>`, before and after side by side in a table, one row per page and view that visibly changed, with one line on what to look at:

   ```markdown
   | Before | After |
   | --- | --- |
   | ![Home, dark, before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/indkhan/Moneo/pr-assets/<pr>/before/home-dark.png) | ![Home, dark, after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/indkhan/Moneo/pr-assets/<pr>/after/home-dark.png) |
   ```

4. **A flow:** GitHub plays a GIF inline but not a video from a branch. If `ffmpeg` is installed, turn the recording into a GIF and embed it: `ffmpeg -i video.webm -vf "fps=10,scale=900:-1" flow.gif`. Otherwise embed a screenshot of each key state. Either way, push the recording too (`video.webm` from `test-results/`) and link it.
5. Open the PR on GitHub and check that every image shows.

Say which pages you covered, what changed in each and what you could not capture and why. If nothing visibly changed, say so and attach nothing.

## 6. Clean up

Stop only the server you started, found by its port and this checkout's path, never by name. Leave `.qa/shots/` in place: cleanup removes instances, never the evidence.

## What changed

The chat mic can now turn speech into text **on this computer**. Voice calls and GPT-Live are untouched.

- **Runtime** (`lib/ai/speech/`): transformers.js (`@huggingface/transformers` 4.3) with onnxruntime-node, in a worker thread (`local-worker.mjs`, started with `new Worker(new URL(...))`). The model loads on first use and the worker ends after 5 idle minutes. A crashed worker fails the waiting recordings, and the next recording starts a fresh one.
  - Whisper gets the workspace vocabulary (`voice-vocabulary.ts`, shared through `promptWithNames`) as its prompt (`<|startofprev|>`), and detects the spoken language itself. transformers.js otherwise forces English on multilingual Whisper.
  - Recordings over 30 s are split into windows. Moonshine has no prompt.
- **Engine**: `localSpeech(ref, runner)` plugs into PR 1's registry. `batchEngines(settings)` now takes the settings. A missing, invalid or failing model falls back to OpenAI with the `fellBack` note, as before.
- **Models**: Moonshine Base (67 MB, English), Whisper Base (80 MB, multilingual incl. German), Whisper Small (252 MB, multilingual) and Distil-Whisper (175 MB, English).
  - Each is pinned to a Hugging Face revision, with every file's size and hash (SHA-256 for LFS files, git blob SHA-1 for small ones).
  - The download manager writes `.part` files, resumes with `Range` (and restarts if the server ignores it), and verifies each file before renaming it into place.
  - Models live in `MONEO_DATA_DIR/speech-models`: `.data/speech-models` on the source install, `<home>/data/speech-models` on desktop.
- **Your own model**: a folder holding a Whisper or Moonshine ONNX model. The folder is checked for `config.json` `model_type`, the tokenizer and preprocessor files, and an encoder/decoder pair in q8, fp32 or fp16.
- **Settings → Voice**: "On this computer" is selectable.
  - The model list shows size, languages and speed, with Download, progress and Retry.
  - "A model you already have": a native **Choose folder…** dialog on desktop (through `lib/desktop-bridge.ts` and `desktop/src/bridge.ts`, refused from a phone because the dialog would open on the computer), or a path field on the source install. Either way, it shows whether a model was found.
  - **Try it** records a sentence and shows what the model heard and how long it took. It calls `/api/voice/models/try`, which reports failures instead of falling back.
- **Stored choice**: `workspace_settings.speech_local_model` (migration `202611160227_speech_local_model.sql`, `save_workspace_preferences` updated, `lib/schema.ts` aligned). Reset all data deletes the settings row, so it clears the choice. It never touches model files.
- **Desktop**:
  - `next.config.ts` traces this platform's onnxruntime-node binary and onnxruntime-common into the standalone server. transformers.js loads them with `createRequire`, so they weren't traced. `build.mjs` fails if the binary is missing.
  - Models are not added to backup/restore: backups hold the database, storage and config only, and models can be downloaded again (noted in `desktop/src/backend/README.md`).
  - `fetch-backend.mjs` needs no change. The native module ships inside the app's `node_modules`, not as a backend service. Fuses are untouched.
- **Source install**: plain `npm ci` works. A new `.npmrc` sets `onnxruntime-node-install=skip` so Linux doesn't download the optional CUDA provider (hundreds of MB) on every install. No new environment variable. README explains downloading and choosing a model.

## Decisions to check

- **q8 for every model, so sizes differ from the issue's estimates** (Whisper Base 80 MB instead of ~150, Whisper Small 252 MB instead of ~500). On this machine, Whisper Base q8 was faster than fp16 (3.6 s vs 4.4 s warm for 7.4 s of audio) with the same or better text, at half the size. onnxruntime's CPU backend gains nothing from fp16.
- **"Choose folder…" instead of "Choose file…"**: transformers.js models are several files (config, tokenizer, two ONNX files), so the owner picks the folder.
- **Intel Macs can't run it**: onnxruntime-node 1.30 ships no darwin-x64 binary. Settings says so, and the mic falls back to OpenAI. The mac-x64 desktop build still builds (the binary check only runs where onnxruntime has one).

- `npm test`: 316 files, 1805 tests passed. New tests:
  - Download manager: fake fetch, full download, resume with `Range`, server ignoring `Range`, hash mismatch never installed, one download per model with progress.
  - Engine selection: fake model runner, own folder, downloaded and partly downloaded suggested models, invalid folders, model failure, all through `transcribeWithFallback`.
  - Worker runner: idle unload, never while busy, crash recovery.
  - Routes: models list and download, try (no fallback), folder picker (desktop only, refused from a phone).
  - Also the bridge route and the settings action.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` (no warnings) and `npm run check:bundle` pass. `/settings` is 282 KB of a 298 KB budget.
- `npm run desktop:build` (Windows) passes. Its `node_modules` runs the packaged worker with Moonshine.
- `lib/schema.live.test.ts` passes against moneo-qa with the migration applied. I then reverted the migration on the shared QA database: column dropped, PR 1's function restored, migration row removed.

  - Whisper Base fp16 with the names as prompt: "…at Netto for groceries, and moved 200 euros from Girokonto to Revolut.", 4.4 s.
  - Whisper Base q8: the same text, 3.6 s.
  - The owner's-own-folder path worked with an absolute Windows path.

  - `/api/voice/session` returned `{"mode":"batch","engine":"local","fellBack":false}` and `/api/voice/transcribe` returned the text with `engine: "local"`.
  - No console errors or failed requests.
